payload.name: Location search via planned landmarks
payload.description: When a question asks for a person's location, US state, or whereabouts during a time period and direct searches do not surface an explicit location, apply this before concluding no information exists.
content: Before answering 'no information', search memory for the person's event/plan memories with world_start inside the target time window, using the person's name with activity or destination keywords found in their existing plans (e.g., visit, lake, trip, kayak).
If any retrieved plan/event names a geographic landmark, use that landmark as a query term in a follow-up search; when the landmark is tied to a state, use that to answer the location question.

Stop after one confirming follow-up if the landmark resolves the location; if the landmark spans multiple states, report those states or use other retrieved context to disambiguate, and do not enumerate landmarks beyond those already present in the retrieved memories.

solves: Generic location queries miss plan/event memories whose named landmarks imply the state. Applies to future 'Which US state was X in during [month/year]?' questions where an event/plan in that window names a place. Exclude cases where direct search already reveals an explicit location, or where no landmark-bearing plan/event exists in the window.
